newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU flour exports dashed by recent refund cuts.
newsitem.headline: EU flour exports dashed by recent refund cuts.

text.p: European Union flour exports were virtually halted by a recent Brussels decision to slash export refunds, latest EU estimates showed on Monday.
Traders' export commitments grew by just 2,000 tonnes in the week to March 11 compared with 200,000 tonnes the week before, figures supplied by member country officials showed.
The latest small increase in the number of export licences taken out by traders brings EU export commitments for soft wheat flour to 5.038 million tonnes between last July 1 and March 11.
The European Commission acted in three stages in the week of March 3 to prevent a run on flour exports by using its power to veto new licences and then twice cutting the export refund.
The latest refund of eight Ecus per tonne is less than the refund offered for unprocessed wheat grain, making flour exports unattractive expect in cases of dire commercial necessity.

EU grain industry sources say the Commission has set itself an informal wheat flour export target of five million tonnes in the year to June 30. But the Brussels-based executive has not itself published any export targets. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5146
